* Lore egg, 17 Oct 2026. Card lore is "Hoth hath no fury like a Wookiee scorned." That is the proverb form "Hell hath no fury like a woman scorned" (''hath'' is the proverb, not Congreve). Congreve, ''The Mourning Bride'' (London: Jacob Tonson, 1697), end of Act III, Zara: "Heav'n has no Rage, like Love to Hatred turn'd, / Nor Hell a Fury, like a Woman scorn'd." Opened 1697 Tonson scan https://archive.org/details/mourningbridetra00cong (Act IV starts printed p. 49). Transcription opened: Wikisource Act III; preserved copy https://web.archive.org/web/20120308172619/https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Mourning_Bride/Act_III
* Marginal: Colley Cibber, ''Love's Last Shift'' (1696) has a similar line ("no Fiend in Hell can match the fury of a disappointed Woman") a year earlier; left out of the article because the card matches the Congreve proverb, not Cibber.
